observable_failures: Despite manually setting the header, `.netrc` is used and overrides it with Basic auth, causing a 401 Unauthorized response.
repair_targets: When set to `false`, `.netrc` credentials are ignored, ensuring that any explicitly set `Authorization` headers are respected.
A new `use_netrc` parameter (defaulting to `true`) has been added to the module and underlying request logic.
The `Authorization` header with `Bearer` should be used and the request should succeed if valid.

semantic_boundaries: Current code handles three auth sources for non-FTP URLs: explicit username/password arguments, credentials embedded in the URL, and fallback `.netrc` credentials; it does not handle a caller-specified opt-out for `.netrc` lookup.
The `.netrc` path is only reached when no explicit username was resolved and the URL lacked embedded credentials; explicit auth takes precedence over `.netrc`.

`.netrc` lookup exceptions are only partially handled: `IOError` during `netrc.netrc(...)` is suppressed to `login = None`, but there is no boundary/control around whether lookup should happen at all.
Current `.netrc` handling applies only on non-FTP requests.
Current `.netrc` fallback is skipped whenever explicit username/password or URL-embedded credentials are present, and also bypassed when `use_gssapi` is enabled.
Current `.netrc` branch silently ignores missing `.netrc` files via `IOError`, and only injects an Authorization header when both username and password are returned.
behavioral_constraints: `Request.open()` resolves auth in order: explicit `url_username`/`url_password`, then credentials embedded in the URL, then GSSAPI/basic-auth handler paths, and only in the final `else` branch falls back to `.netrc`; callers currently depend on this auth resolution flow.

When `.netrc` lookup succeeds, `Request.open()` injects an `Authorization` header directly before opener construction; any stored constructor preference must be consulted before this point to affect outgoing requests.

`fetch_url()` derives request settings from `module.params` and passes them through `open_url()`; module-level support for any new `.netrc` control must be threaded through this chain rather than handled only inside `uri`.
Header dictionaries are merged as `dict(self.headers, **headers)` before auth handling, so request-specific headers override instance headers and auth injection happens after that merge.
Auth branch ordering matters: explicit `url_username` / URL-embedded credentials are handled before the `.netrc` fallback branch, and `use_gssapi` bypasses both basic-auth and `.netrc` logic.
`.netrc` lookup is only reached for non-FTP requests and only when neither explicit username nor URL netloc credentials were resolved.
backward_compatibility: `Request.__init__` currently accepts the existing keyword parameters (`headers`, `use_proxy`, `force`, `timeout`, `validate_certs`, `url_username`, `url_password`, `http_agent`, `force_basic_auth`, `follow_redirects`, `client_cert`, `client_key`, `cookies`, `unix_socket`, `ca_path`, `unredirected_headers`, `decompress`, `ciphers`); existing callers such as `open_url()` rely on that signature remaining compatible.

`open_url()` and `fetch_url()` currently default to consulting `.netrc` when no explicit username is supplied; any fix should preserve current behavior unless the new control parameter is explicitly set to disable it.

`url_argument_spec()` is the shared parameter source for modules like `uri`; extending auth behavior should preserve existing parameter names and defaults so existing playbooks continue to work unchanged.

`Request.open` currently accepts the documented kwargs shown in its signature; adding `.netrc` control must preserve existing parameters and the current fallback pattern where per-call `None` inherits instance defaults (`_fallback`).

`open_url` is a public helper that forwards many auth-related kwargs directly to `Request().open`; any fix must keep this wrapper/call signature behavior compatible for existing callers such as lookup/url and galaxy code.

Current callers can omit any `.netrc` setting and still receive `.netrc`-derived Basic authorization when no explicit credentials are provided; changing default behavior would be externally observable.
similar_implementation_patterns: `Request` already uses a constructor-store plus per-call fallback pattern for options such as `force_basic_auth`, `follow_redirects`, `client_cert`, `ca_path`, `decompress`, and `ciphers` (`lib/ansible/module_utils/urls.py:1332-1347`, `1416-1432`). A `.netrc` preference would fit this existing pattern.
`fetch_url()` already reads auth-related module params and forwards them to `open_url()` (`lib/ansible/module_utils/urls.py:1881-1905`), which is the existing propagation style for request options.

`Request.open` already uses a standard per-call-overrides-instance-default pattern through `_fallback` for auth-adjacent controls such as `force_basic_auth` (lib/ansible/module_utils/urls.py:1416-1432).
`open_url` mirrors `Request.open` parameters and forwards them directly, providing the existing pattern for exposing new request controls to callers (lib/ansible/module_utils/urls.py:1649-1668).

Galaxy API auth avoids overwriting an existing `Authorization` header (`lib/ansible/galaxy/api.py:418-421`), a relevant reference for preserving explicit caller auth precedence when adjusting auth sourcing.

If a `.netrc` control is added to `open_url()` -> `fetch_url()` must pass it through.
If module users must control `.netrc` behavior -> `url_argument_spec()` and modules such as `lib/ansible/modules/uri.py` that consume it must be updated together.

dependency_propagation: Shared URL consumers inherit behavior through `url_argument_spec()` -> `fetch_url()` -> `open_url()` -> `Request.open()`, so adding `.netrc` control at the constructor level also has implications for helper functions and module argument plumbing.

The `uri` module builds its argument spec from `url_argument_spec()`, so any module-facing toggle for `.netrc` use would naturally propagate from `lib/ansible/module_utils/urls.py` into `lib/ansible/modules/uri.py`.
A `.netrc` control would need propagation across `Request.__init__`, `Request.open`, and the `open_url` wrapper to preserve the module_utils URL API shape.
Higher-level callers such as `lookup/url.py` and `fetch_url` currently expose/pass auth-related controls only through `open_url`; without wrapper propagation they cannot influence `.netrc` behavior.

requirements.text: - `Request.__init__` must expose a parameter that determines if `.netrc` credentials are considered and store that preference for later use in request handling.
requirements.findings: `Request.__init__` in `lib/ansible/module_utils/urls.py` does not expose any parameter controlling whether `.netrc` credentials should be consulted. Its constructor accepts auth-related parameters such as `url_username`, `url_password`, and `force_basic_auth`, but no `use_netrc`-style flag, and it stores only those existing constructor inputs on `self`. In `Request.open`, when no explicit username is available and the URL does not embed credentials, the code unconditionally attempts `netrc.netrc(...).authenticators(parsed.hostname)` and, if found, sets an `Authorization` header from those credentials. There is no constructor-stored preference used to suppress this behavior later in request handling. The higher-level helpers `open_url`, `fetch_url`, `url_argument_spec`, and the `uri` module likewise expose no `.netrc` control parameter to pass through.

requirements.text: - `Request.open` should accept a control for `.netrc` usage, apply fallback when not provided, and only attempt to read `.netrc` if allowed.
requirements.findings: `Request.open` currently has no parameter controlling `.netrc` usage. It applies fallback only for existing kwargs such as `force_basic_auth`, but there is no corresponding `.netrc` control in either `Request.__init__`, `Request.open`, or `open_url`. In the no-username/no-netloc-credentials branch, `Request.open` unconditionally attempts `netrc.netrc(os.environ.get('NETRC'))` and only suppresses `IOError`; therefore `.netrc` is always consulted for non-FTP requests when explicit credentials are absent, rather than only when allowed by a caller-provided control. Existing tests verify this unconditional `.netrc` authorization behavior.

requirements.text: - `open_url` has to define a parameter for `.netrc` handling, default it to enabled, and forward the value when creating a `Request`.
- `fetch_url` needs to accept a parameter that signals whether `.netrc` is used, default it to enabled, and pass it along to `open_url`.
- `url_get` should define a parameter for `.netrc` usage and explicitly forward this preference to `fetch_url` in all calls.
- The main flow of `get_url` must retrieve the `.netrc` setting from module arguments and consistently forward it to `url_get` for both primary download and checksum retrieval.
- The `uri` function requires a parameter controlling `.netrc` behavior and should propagate it to the lower-level request call.
- The entry point of `uri` has to include `.netrc` in its accepted arguments and forward the captured value into the `uri` function.
- The `run` method of the `url` lookup plugin must respect the configured `.netrc` option and forward it to the underlying request logic.
